newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Axa/UAP's Colonia posts 1996 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Axa/UAP's Colonia posts 1996 profit rise.

text.p: CKAG Colonia Konzern AG, the German insurer now part of France's giant Axa group, on Tuesday said an efficiency drive, modest costs and a capital markets boom lifted its 1996 net profit by 12 percent.

The insurer, which plans to change the name of its umbrella holding company this year to Axa-Colonia Konzern AG, reported net profit of 236 million marks ($138.6 million) for 1996 and said the strong earnings trend should continue this year.

In a letter to shareholders, Colonia pledged to continue its cost-cutting efforts this year and predicted that economic conditions should improve somewhat, although factors like Germany's record unemployment would continue to dampen growth.
"Overall we are confident that we will achieve a group result for 1997 that will continue from the good result of the previous year," the company said.

Colonia also said it planned to raise its dividend payout by what analysts noted was a surprisingly generous 20 percent, with the common share payout rising to 34 percent, or 1.70 marks, from 28 percent.

"I think this may have some connection with its new parent," commented BHF Bank AG analyst Dieter Hein on the dividend hike. "In the past, Colonia has had the habit of storing much of its profits in reserves."

Colonia acquired its new French parent last year when Axa began a takeover of its majority-owner Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP), knocking Germany's Allianz AG Holding off its position as Europe's top insurer.
The companies will start releasing combined earnings as of the 1997 financial year.
